title: Ramayana Trailer Set for July 24 Global Premiere as Two Versions Clear CBFC Certification
excerpt: The most anticipated Bollywood film of the year unveils its first full trailer next week, with a 4-minute-15-second cut receiving a 'U' certificate and a massive marketing campaign spanning 400 schools.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Ramayana trailer premieres globally on July 24, running 4 minutes 15 seconds.
  • Two versions of the trailer received a 'U' certificate from CBFC on July 15.
  • The film features a star-studded cast including Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi.
  • Part 1 is set for a Diwali 2026 release, with Part 2 in 2027.
  • A marketing campaign reached five lakh students across 400 schools in India.

  • The Ramayana trailer, running 4 minutes 15 seconds, received a 'U' certificate from the CBFC on July 15 — the longest trailer for an Indian film in recent memory.
  • Two versions have been censored: a full 'Trailer' and a slightly shorter 'Theatrical Trailer,' with the global digital premiere set for July 24.
  • The star cast includes Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Sunny Deol as Hanuman, with music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.
  • Part 1 releases on Diwali 2026 (November 6), with Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027.

The countdown to what may be Indian cinema's biggest spectacle in a generation enters its final stretch next Thursday. The Central Board of Film Certification cleared two versions of the Ramayana trailer on July 15, setting up a global premiere on July 24 that the makers are positioning as a watershed moment for Bollywood's ambitions on the world stage.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PkdpvVi6WhA

At 4 minutes and 15 seconds, the longer version is unusually expansive by industry standards — closer to a short film than a conventional trailer. A second cut, labeled 'Theatrical Trailer,' runs four minutes flat. Both received 'U' (universal) certificates, the CBFC's unrestricted rating. Which version drops online remains to be seen, but the sheer length signals the producers' confidence in the material.

"Before the trailer, the makers ran the "Colours of Ramayana" art competition across 400 schools in 18 Indian cities, reaching an estimated five lakh students."

An Ensemble Built for Scale

Director Nitesh Tiwari, whose Dangal remains one of the highest-grossing Indian films ever made, has assembled a cast designed to pull audiences across linguistic and regional lines. Ranbir Kapoor takes on the role of Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Kannada superstar Yash portrays Ravana, and Sunny Deol brings his screen presence to Lord Hanuman. Ravi Dubey completes the central group as Lakshman.

The supporting cast reads like a who's who of Indian cinema: Arun Govil — who played Lord Rama in the definitive 1987 television series that brought the country to a standstill — joins alongside Lara Dutta, Vivek Oberoi, Kajal Aggarwal, and Rakul Preet Singh.

The score combines two of the most decorated composers working today. A.R. Rahman, Oscar winner for Slumdog Millionaire, handles the Indian musical palette, while Hans Zimmer — whose credits include Inception, The Dark Knight, and Dune — brings his orchestral sensibility. It is one of the rare instances of a Hollywood A-list composer collaborating on an Indian production.

A Marketing Machine in Motion

Ramayana's promotional campaign has already broken from Bollywood convention. Before the trailer, the makers ran the "Colours of Ramayana" art competition across 400 schools in 18 Indian cities, reaching an estimated five lakh students. Winners receive limited-edition merchandise and the chance to watch the trailer in 3D theatres before anyone else.

Reports suggest the trailer may also debut at San Diego Comic-Con, which would mark the first time a Bollywood film has used the world's largest pop culture convention as a launchpad. Warner Bros. is reportedly handling international distribution, giving the project global theatrical infrastructure that few Indian films have ever accessed.

"This is not just a film. It is the telling of a story that has shaped a civilization for thousands of years."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer

What's at Stake

Producer Namit Malhotra has called the project a two-decade dream. The production budget, while not officially disclosed, is widely reported to be among the highest ever for an Indian film. Part 1 is scheduled for a Diwali release on November 6, 2026, with Part 2 arriving the following Diwali.

A Marketing Campaign Like No Other
›Reached five lakh students
›400 schools in 18 cities
›Winners get exclusive merchandise

The trailer reveal is the third promotional asset after an introduction clip in July 2025 and a teaser titled "Rama" released on Hanuman Jayanti in April. Both generated massive online engagement but also drew scrutiny over VFX quality — a deliberately unfinished sequence in the introduction clip was mistaken for the final product, sparking debate before the makers clarified.

For the Indian diaspora, the Ramayana holds a significance that goes beyond entertainment. The epic is foundational to cultural and spiritual identity across the global Hindu community, and a cinematic adaptation of this scale — with world-class production values, international distribution, and crossover composers — represents a moment the community has long anticipated.
